maya: Heads-up — p95 spiked after yesterday's kernel switchover on the raptor family. Opening a thread to collect profiling + quick mitigation ideas. :eyes:
chris: How big was the spike and which route/tier?
maya: Quick numbers from last-night run: chat.standard route, seq=512 workload. p95 went 210ms -> 360ms. Microbatch sizes dropped and queue wait time increased. Kernel changed from `fused_matmul_v1` -> `fused_matmul_v2`.
---
maya: Raw perf snippet from the profiler (filtered):
```
route: chat.standard
seq: 512
old_kernel: fused_matmul_v1, p95=210ms, avg_batch=7.2
new_kernel: fused_matmul_v2, p95=360ms, avg_batch=4.1
queue_wait_p95: 45ms -> 120ms
kv_miss_rate: 2.3% -> 7.8%
```
---
tomas: That looks like kernel cost + reduced batching caused backlog. Two quick ideas: 1) kernel-aware queue weights so heavier kernels get lower initial token budgets; 2) token-credit decay so routes that cause high kv_miss get temporary budget shrink.
chris: +1 for kernel-aware weights. Can you sketch a simple allocator?
tomas: Pseudo:```
for incoming req:
  kernel_cost = kernel_cost_estimator(req.model, seq)
  tier_factor = route_tier[to] # e.g., prod=1.0, standard=0.9
  target_tokens = clamp(base_tokens / kernel_cost * tier_factor, min=8, max=256)
  enqueue(req, budget=target_tokens)
```
This biases microbatches to form larger batches for cheap kernels and keeps expensive ones small to protect p95.
sara: Also we should consider KV cache behavior. The spike in kv_miss_rate suggests routing changed shards or cache keys invalidated after the kernel rollout. If cache warms slowly, expensive kernels amplify queueing. Recommend short warmup windows + prefetch for known-hot prefixes.
chris: Good call. Metric set to track for the experiment: `p95_lat_route`, `avg_batch_size`, `queue_wait_p95`, `kv_miss_rate`, `tokens_consumed_per_req`. We'll do canary by route tier (non-prod -> standard -> prod).
maya: Proposed experiment config snippet (canary):
```json
{"experiment": "kernel-aware-queue-weighting-v1", "stages": ["staging","standard"], "controls": {"base_tokens": 64, "min_tokens": 8}, "policy": "kernel_cost_inverse", "observables": ["p95_lat_route","kv_miss_rate","avg_batch_size"]}
```
chris: Rollout plan: 1) staging 10% traffic 2) monitor 30m 3) expand to standard 20% if p95 delta < 5% and kv_miss_rate decrease/unchanged. Otherwise rollback.
perf-bot: Baseline snapshot uploaded: `s3://perf-bench/chat-standard/baseline-2178900000.json` (p95=210ms, kv_miss=2.3%, avg_batch=7.2).
maya: I'll own the staging run. @tomas please implement kernel_cost_estimator prototype and a toggle in the batcher. @sara please add KV warmup flag for the route. We'll reconvene after the 30m staging window. Thanks all :thumbsup:
